Two mismatched flags in one card -- the SAME mistake as card/disintegration, and the same verdict (rule 3). Live for the first flag the moment an in-combat generator is pointed at a pool including statuses.

OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): Divergence (1) closed: the cost bump is per-COMBAT. FranticEscape.cs:45 is `EnergyCost.AddThisCombat(1)`, a LocalCostModifier with EndOfCombat expiration, and the port mutated `self._energy_cost`, the card's BASE cost -- which `reset_combat_state` does not re-seed, because it does not re-run `_init_vars`. It now calls `set_cost_this_combat(self.energy_cost + 1)`, the field `reset_combat_state` already clears. EXECUTED: played twice the card reads 3, and after `reset_combat_state` it is back to 1 where it used to start the next combat at 3.  Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps.py.  NOT CLOSED: divergence (2), the Apply-vs-ModifyAmount substitution and the missing `s.Target == Owner.Creature` filter, which this entry already records as DORMANT -- single-player means one Sandpit can only target the one player, so the filter selects the same instance.  The text it replaced read: TWO DIVERGENCES. (1) THE COST BUMP IS PERMANENT IN THE SIM. `base.EnergyCost.AddThisCombat(1)` (FranticEscape.cs:45) registers a LocalCostModifier with `LocalCostModifierExpiration.EndOfCombat` (CardEnergyCost.cs, the AddThisCombat overload), so the card resets to cost 1 in the NEXT combat. The sim writes `self._energy_cost += 1` (frantic_escape.py:42), mutating the card's BASE cost -- and `_energy_cost` is re-seeded only by `_init_vars`, which `reset_combat_state` (cards/base.py:239-245) does not call. So a Frantic Escape played twice in one combat and then carried into the next starts that combat at cost 3 in the sim and cost 1 in the game. LIVE: The Insatiable's LIQUIFY_GROUND adds these cards, the sim keeps deck cards across combats (RunState.deck), and `reset_combat_state` exists precisely to clear per-combat cost state -- it already handles `_cost_this_combat`, which is the field this should have used (`set_cost_this_combat` is a SET, so an ADD needs `self.set_cost_this_combat(self._energy_cost + 1)` or an equivalent per-combat delta). (2) APPLY vs MODIFYAMOUNT AND A MISSING TARGET FILTER: C# finds the Sandpit power `s.Target == Owner.Creature` (FranticEscape.cs:40) and calls `PowerCmd.ModifyAmount(sandpitPower, 1m, sandpitEnemy, this)` on that exact instance; the sim takes the first enemy with ANY `sandpit` power and calls `PowerCmd.apply(..., SandpitPower, 1)` (frantic_escape.py:36-40), which routes through the stacking path and, unlike ModifyAmount, runs the full apply pipeline. DORMANT: single-player means one Sandpit can only target the one player, so the `Target ==` filter selects the same instance, and the sim's `PowerCmd.apply` reaches `existing.on_stack(amount)` (cmds.py:308-322) for an already-present power, which is ModifyAmount's job. Live if a second Sandpit or a multi-target Sandpit is ever reachable.

guards.rationale: Both take the first match and stop. The sim's extra liveness filter is not the card/bash family -- it selects which creature to affect rather than gating an effect on an already-chosen one, and C#'s `Enemies` list has already had removed corpses taken out of it (CreatureCmd.cs:523-525).
